speaker: Doctor
text: I am sorry, but there seems to be a misunderstanding. As Dr. Agent, I am the doctor, and you are the patient. Please describe your symptoms or the symptoms you are experiencing for your infant to help me start my assessment.

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any "barking" cough or hoarseness associated with these breathing episodes, and does the child have a family history of thyroid issues? REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. (Note: The patient's age and symptoms of stridor worsening with neck flexion and crying are classic for laryngomalacia; Multiple Sclerosis is not a diagnosis for an infant and does not present this way.)
